subject: Gridline renewal — support tier, committed capacity, and latency SLOs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@gridline.com>, Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@gridline.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Gridline renewal — support tier, committed capacity, and latency SLOs

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the productive renewal call today. Per our conversation I put together two practical paths for your Q3 renewal that balance cost and operational guarantees:

Option A — Standard renewal + ops credits
- 12 month term
- No commitment change (renew at current TUs)
- Standard support (business hours) + $25k ops credit for migration and testing
- No formal latency SLO in the contract (benchmarked guidance only)

Option B — Premium SLA (recommended)
- 12 month term, 20% committed increase over current monthly usage (committed capacity)
- Premium support (24/7 Pager + 1-hour P1 response target)
- Contracted Latency SLO: P95 <= 350ms on dedicated capacity; credit structure for breaches
- 10% renewal discount in exchange for the committed increase and auto-renew clause
- Onboarding window: 4 weeks for capacity provisioning + 2-week smoke test

Attached: redwood_premium_sla_addendum_v1.pdf and a blank committed capacity workbook for your team to fill out.

Next steps: if Option B looks viable, can you confirm the committed throughput (baseline monthly token/embedding estimate) and procurement timelines? If procurement needs a PO and a Work Order, let me know — we can accelerate.

If useful, I can loop in Lauren (sales lead) and Sergio (Customer Ops) to confirm the operational and discount approvals.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0121

Attachments: redwood_premium_sla_addendum_v1.pdf (application/pdf), gridline_committed_capacity_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Elena Morales <elena@gridline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@gridline.com>, procurement@gridline.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gridline renewal — support tier, committed capacity, and latency SLOs

Ben,

Thanks for the clear options — appreciate the quick follow-up. A few clarifying questions before we share with procurement: 

1) Latency SLO: we need P95 <= 300ms for our customer-facing API during business hours in us-west. Is that achievable with your dedicated capacity option or would that require extra engineering work / larger commitment?

2) Uptime: can you commit to 99.95% availability for the API endpoint in the SLA? If not, what uptime is realistic for Premium SLA?

3) Credits: please send the exact credit formula for SLA breaches so procurement can model worst-case exposure.

4) Ramp: if we agree to the 20% committed increase, what's the fastest provisioning schedule to have production-ready capacity? We prefer a soft-launch by Aug 1 if possible.

Procurement has indicated they prefer a single 12-month PO; timing target for signature is mid-June if we can get terms nailed.

Thanks — Elena

Elena Morales
Director of Product | Gridline Health
elena@gridline.com | +1 617-555-0987

Elena — thanks, good questions. Looping in Lauren and Sergio to confirm the commitments and timeline.

Lauren: can we approve a 10% one-time renewal discount in exchange for a 12-month commitment at +20% throughput? Procurement is aiming for mid-June signature so this would be a small concession to close Q2 ARR.

Sergio: can you confirm whether we can reach P95 <= 300ms in us-west with dedicated capacity, and what minimum GPU pool size you’d recommend for Gridline's traffic profile? Also need the exact uptime target we can offer and the credit table for SLA breaches.

Elena / Tom — I’ll consolidate answers and follow up with a single redline-ready addendum.

-Ben

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@gridline.com>, Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@gridline.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gridline renewal — support tier, committed capacity, and latency SLOs

Hi team — thanks for the details, Elena. Quick operational answers below.

1) Latency (P95): With a dedicated GPU pool sized to your monthly throughput + 20% buffer, we can commit to P95 <= 320-340ms across typical request mixes. Achieving P95 <= 300ms is possible but requires either a modest increase to the committed reserve (~+10% on top of the +20%) or a short CDN/edge-proxy optimization for static prefix traffic. We recommend we model both options in the workbook you received.

2) Uptime: For Premium SLA on dedicated capacity we offer 99.9% financially-backed availability for the control plane + inference endpoints in a region. 99.95% is attainable with an active multi-availability-zone deployment and additional routing fallbacks; that is an elevated configuration (and price tier) because it requires cross-AZ duplication.

3) Credits formula: see attached SLA addendum excerpt — in short: credits scale by severity and outage minutes; e.g., for availability below 99.9% credit = (monthly fee * proportion of minutes below threshold * 0.5), with escalation tiers for repeated breaches. I attached a redwood_premium_sla_addendum_v1.pdf containing the full table.

4) Provisioning timeline: once contract signed, we can provision a dedicated pool in 10 business days; smoke tests and traffic validation add 7 business days. That aligns with an Aug 1 soft-launch if we sign by Jun 15 and share committed usage by Jun 8.

Operational notes:
- We will allocate a named SRE on the account for the onboarding window and two weeks post-launch.
- Canary routing and prefix caching will be enabled during ramp to reduce cold-start latencies.
- We recommend a one-week performance validation with your engineering team during the smoke test.

Happy to walk through the committed capacity workbook with your infra lead — suggest a 30-minute sync this week.

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez
Head of Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_premium_sla_addendum_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700

Elena / Tom — quick wrap: Lauren approved the 10% renewal discount in exchange for the 12-month +20% committed capacity. We also confirmed the standard Premium SLA credit formula and the operational timeline above.

I uploaded the redline-ready Premium SLA addendum (redwood_premium_sla_addendum_v1.pdf) to the deal and started a DocuSign envelope so procurement can sign the PO + SLA in one flow: https://app.docusign.com/sign/ABCD1234.

Requested items from Gridline to finalize:
- Completed committed capacity workbook (return by Tue, Jun 8)
- Procurement contact or PO reference (for DocuSign)
- Confirmation whether you want the multi-AZ availability option (99.95%) or single-region premium (99.9%).

If we get the workbook and PO info by Jun 8 we can provision in time for an Aug 1 soft-launch as requested. If procurement needs an internal pricing justification, I can provide a cost/benefit breakdown showing expected unit cost reduction from caching + batching with dedicated capacity.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0121
